deltas.purpose: Desktop "/" command menu for agent DMs (Claude Code style). Only in a 1:1 DM whose other member is an agent (any composer except edit, including replies and the Inbox detail pane), typing "/" at any word start in the composer (like @ and #; never inside a word, URL, email or path) opens a menu filtered as you type (prefix then substring matches; arrows move, Tab/Enter choose, Esc closes; click chooses). The list comes from the guest route's GET /agents/<agent pubkey>/commands, signed natively with NIP-98 (kind 27235, u = exact URL, method GET) by the signed-in user with X-Buzz-Community, fetched lazily the first time the menu opens for an agent and cached per agent key with the ETag (If-None-Match revalidation at most once a minute; 304 keeps the list). The body is validated (contract_version 1, same agent key; session commands only new/sessions, skills with a bounded name and skill_id; skills shadowing a session command dropped); any error (403 identity_not_linked, 404 agent_not_found, timeout, invalid body) shows no menu and is not retried in a loop. Session commands appear only when listed; choosing /sessions sends it as the same plain message as before, and choosing /new first asks "Start a new session?" (Start sends /new, Cancel sends nothing). Choosing a skill puts "/<name> " in the composer with its argument_hint shown until arguments are typed; on send, a listed skill invocation goes out as one user-signed kind 9 top-level message with content "/<name> <args>" and exactly one ["buzz-skill", skill_id, args] tag (args trimmed, at most 4000 characters, refused visibly when longer), addressed to the DM members like the composer; the composer and its draft clear only after a successful send. The cache is cleared in resetCommunityState(). Hooks: one module plus re-export in extensions/mod.rs, one use line and one command registration in lib.rs, and the menu, key handling, query update and skill send in MessageComposer.tsx. In channels and threads (not forums, not threads inside a 1:1 DM) the "/" may follow a leading mention of the agent it is for; otherwise it is for the agent the conversation addresses or its only agent, and with several the menu offers them first. The group list (?audience=group) never offers personal skills, and offers session commands only to the agent's owner. A picked group skill keeps its typed text, mentions the agent and adds a validated ["buzz-skill", id, args] tag; a group session command is sent as the bare command addressed with a p tag. The menu lists every command the server returns (up to 1200), ranked as you type; when the server marks the list truncated, typing also asks ?q=<text> (trimmed, lowercased, at most 64 characters, cached a minute per query) and merges the matches. With several agents, agents whose list is known to be empty are not offered, one remaining agent is used directly, a typed name that matches no agent still lists them all, and choosing an agent keeps the typed text. Agent detection for the menu (useSlashAgentPredicate.ts) also counts directory agents, agent-role channel members and agent profiles. A skill picked mid-message is still the one skill invocation, with the rest of the message as its input; a second pick replaces the first; session commands are offered only for a leading "/".

A build-time VITE_BUZZ_PREFERRED_RUN_ON names a bundled destination: when that provider is discovered, 'Where it runs' leads the create form with exactly that destination (default) or this computer, plain labels, prefilled name and instructions, and no untrusted-binary warning for the provider shipped inside the signed app bundle. Provider protocol v2 gains an optional read-only 'preflight' lifecycle operation (owner-signed kind-27236 proof) so the dialog can show owner readiness, a Connect action and a one-line notice, and block Create until ready. Deploy failures may carry remote_state 'absent'. A failed remote start is rolled back: confirmed delete when an agent id is known, otherwise one replay of the idempotent deploy to learn it; the local record and key are kept unless the provider confirmed deletion or absence. A conditionally shown bounded provider field (x-visible-when with options) must hold a current option before Create, and an empty option list renders an explicit empty state instead of a blank dropdown.
deltas.upstreamStatus: Generic provider protocol and create-flow improvements; candidate for upstream.
deltas.removalCondition: Remove when block/buzz offers a build-preferred run destination, provider preflight, and confirmed rollback of failed remote creates.

deltas.purpose: Mobile owner review of agent guest-access approvals, matching the desktop approval card. Tapping a 46040 request in the Activity inbox opens a review sheet that fetches the approval from the hosted guest route (the system of record) with a native NIP-98 owner client (X-Buzz-Community = active relay host) and shows who is asking (TEST badge, route-classified kind, link state, linked-ago, first/Nth request), the venue, the exact draft, data used and plain-language hold reasons, a sources picker for owner-data requests with nothing pre-ticked when the request named none, a grant scope, and a preview sentence that follows the owner's current choices. Approve / Edit then approve (write the reply myself) / Deny / Deny and block record the decision first, then send the owner-signed NIP-44 observer control frame; a decided request leaves the inbox at once. 46042 alerts open their text. The route is the build-time --dart-define BUZZ_GUEST_ROUTE_URL and is used only while the community it serves (BUZZ_GUEST_ROUTE_RELAY_URL, default BUZZ_RELAY_URL) is active; without it the sheet says to review on desktop. The upstream inbox page carries one open hook.

deltas.purpose: Claude-Code-style "/" autocomplete in a 1:1 agent DM: typing "/" at any word start in the composer (like @ and #; never inside a word, URL, email or path) opens a popup of the agent's conversation commands (/new, /sessions, listed only where the server says session controls are on) and the skills the agent can use, read lazily from the hosted guest route's NIP-98 GET /agents/{key}/commands (ETag revalidated, cached 5 minutes per agent, any failure shows no popup). Picking a skill inserts /<name> and, on send, adds exactly one ["buzz-skill", skill_id, args] tag so the provider runs the skill natively instead of the agent reading prose; a typed-by-hand name stays an ordinary message. Hooks: the composer's suggestion panel, send tags and clear in compose_bar_widget.dart and helpers.dart, and the agent key passed by already-classified channel_detail_page.dart. Kiingo W6. Opening a 1:1 agent DM also sends a fire-and-forget NIP-98 POST /agents/{key}/prewarm (at most once per agent per 2 minutes) so the server can warm the reader's session; the server always answers 200 and decides. In channels and threads (not forums, not threads inside a 1:1 DM) the "/" may follow a leading mention of the agent it is for; otherwise it is for the agent the conversation addresses or its only agent, and with several the menu offers them first. The group list (?audience=group) never offers personal skills, and offers session commands only to the agent's owner. A picked group skill keeps its typed text, mentions the agent and adds a validated ["buzz-skill", id, args] tag; a group session command is sent as the bare command addressed with a p tag. The popup lists every command the server returns (up to 1200); when the server marks the list truncated, typing also asks ?q=<text> and merges the matches. With several agents, agents whose list is known to be empty are not offered, one remaining agent is used directly, and choosing an agent keeps the typed text. A skill picked mid-message is still the one skill invocation, with the rest of the message as its input; a second pick replaces the first; session commands are offered only for a leading "/". The "#" channel trigger also opens after an opening bracket or tab, matching "@".
deltas.removalCondition: Drop when upstream Buzz ships a provider command/skill autocomplete for agent DMs.
deltas.upstreamStatus: Generic hosted-provider command catalog; not yet submitted to block/buzz.

deltas.purpose: Mobile creation and management of hosted agents, matching the desktop create flow. The phone has no provider binary, so a native Dart client speaks the same provisioning contract the desktop's bundled provider uses: GET /capabilities (Ed25519 catalog pinned by the build-time key, validity window, API-base check), POST /preflight and POST /agents/confirmed-delete with owner-signed kind-27236 proofs (buzz-provider-preflight-v1 / buzz-provider-delete-v1, exact ordered tags), and POST /agents with the standard NIP-OA owner attestation and an x25519-chacha20poly1305 identity envelope (v2 bundle: key plus attestation) sealed to the catalog's provisioning key. The agent key is generated in memory per create and dropped afterwards; it is never stored. The create form leads with Where it runs, renders the provider schema generically (harness, model mode, model family/version, reasoning, tier) with the desktop's visibility, option-filter, reconcile and unmet-choice rules, gates Create on a fresh ready preflight of the current configuration (re-checked on resume and Check again), and rolls back a failed create (confirmed delete with a known id; otherwise one identical idempotent replay then delete; agent_state absent is the only proof of absence; an unconfirmed cleanup is kept in memory and retried before the next create). On success it publishes the agent's kind:0 (agent NIP-98 plus x-auth-tag) and the owner's kind:30177, and remembers the public record; delete retires both (kind:5 plus NIP-IA 9035). Management uses the owner-key routes POST /owner/agents/list, /owner/agents/update and /owner/agents/control with buzz-provider-owner-v1 proofs (list: 5 tags; writes: 7 tags binding the agent and the SHA-256 of the canonical body), a fresh single-use proof per attempt and a fixed request id for idempotent retries: the Agents page lists every hosted agent with live state (desktop-created included), pauses/resumes, checks status, reconciles, edits name, instructions, harness and model through the same schema form and preflight (a revision conflict refreshes and asks to save again; lifecycle actions retry once on the newest revision), and deletes any of them through confirmed delete plus the desktop's kind:30177 tombstone and NIP-IA archive. The owner's other kind:30177 agents are listed read-only. Configuration is build-time only: BUZZ_HOSTED_AGENTS_URL, BUZZ_HOSTED_AGENTS_CATALOG_KEY, BUZZ_HOSTED_AGENTS_LOCATION and BUZZ_HOSTED_AGENTS_RELAY_URL (default BUZZ_RELAY_URL), gated to the community it serves. Upstream hooks: one optional Settings page builder and row part, the app.dart builder line (app.dart is classified with the push-tap delta), and the pure-Dart cryptography dependency.
deltas.upstreamStatus: Generic mechanism configured entirely by build-time values; not yet proposed upstream.
deltas.removalCondition: Remove when block/buzz ships hosted-agent creation and management on mobile.

deltas.purpose: Desktop remote signer (Kiingo design mcp-buzz-module.md section 7): a broker next to the build-time guest route (its /buzz-signer/v1 sibling, or BUZZ_DESKTOP_REMOTE_SIGNER_URL) can ask this device to sign as the user. A Rust long-poller (GET /requests?wait_ms=25000, one request in flight, backoff on errors) runs only while the app runs and the per-device, per-community switch 'Allow Kiingo to request signatures' (off by default) is on; every broker call is NIP-98 signed by the user's key with the guest route's X-Buzz-Community. Each request is validated in the backend before anything is shown: signer and event pubkey are the user's own, the expected event id matches the computed id, relay_url is the connected relay's /events or /query, publish kinds are 9/7/40003/9005 (never 0, 10100, 30315, 9000-9002, 9007, 9008, 9030-9032, 27235, 27236, 24243, 1059, identity-rotation kinds or NIP-OA auth tags), only h/e/p/k tags, the h tag equals the displayed channel, the action matches the kind, edits and deletes target the user's own message, read filters stay within the read kinds, and expired requests are skipped; anything else is declined and never signed. A consent modal shows 'Signing as: You (<name>)' distinct from agents, the locally derived action, the channel resolved locally with member count or DM peer, full content or read scope, kind and the requesting client/agent, with Allow once, Deny and Allow for... (kinds in this channel, or reads in this channel or all channels, for 15 min/1 h/8 h). Scopes are created only from the prompt and stored only in the app data dir (remote-signer.json), auto-approve with decision_source scope:<id>, are listed in Settings, Kiingo signing with per-scope revoke, and a top-chrome pill ('Kiingo can sign as you, N scopes') offers one-click revoke of all. A local signing log records time, action, channel, decision and outcome event id (no signatures). Signing (the exact event plus the relay NIP-98 header over the exact body) happens in Rust; the renderer receives display data only. Upstream files carry a module/command registration, the dialog host mount and the settings section hook.
deltas.upstreamStatus: Generic mechanism configured by the build-time guest route URL; Kiingo naming only in added files; not proposed upstream.
deltas.removalCondition: Remove when block/buzz ships a remote signer (NIP-46 or equivalent) with device-local consent scopes, or when Kiingo moves remote signing to relay-native NIP-46.

deltas.purpose: Owner-key re-link for hosted agents, desktop and mobile. After an owner rotates their Buzz key, a hosted provider can still hold their agents under the earlier key. The provider's POST /owner/agents/list answer now carries owner_public_key per agent; an agent is offered for re-link only when that key is present and differs from the signed-in key (null is never stale; deleted agents are skipped). The owner reviews the stale agents with checkboxes (all selected), and only their confirm tap signs: one fresh request id, one NIP-OA owner attestation (compact ["auth",owner,"",sig]) per selected agent and no other, and one fresh single-use kind-27236 buzz-provider-owner-v1 proof with exactly action=rebind_owner_key, provider, request, agent="", community, payload (SHA-256 of the canonical body without the proof) and expires (5 minutes), sent to POST /owner/agents/rebind-owner-key. Nothing retries on its own; a retry is another tap that sends only the retryable agents (profile_revision_conflict, rebind_failed, or an agent the answer omitted) with a new request and proof. Answers are bound to the request id, the current owner key and exactly the requested agents; each agent's outcome is shown in plain words (Re-linked, Already linked, or a one-sentence reason) and whole-request errors as one sentence. Desktop signs and calls the API natively (provider-neutral extension; API base and provider id come from BUZZ_BUILD_HOSTED_AGENTS_URL / BUZZ_BUILD_HOSTED_PROVIDER_ID, falling back to the release composition's BUZZ_HOSTED_API_BASE_URL / BUZZ_PROVIDER_ID; hidden when either is unset) and shows the card in Profile settings through the existing AccountLinkCard mount; mobile adds it to the Agents page. Hooks: two extension re-exports and three command registrations in lib.rs/extensions/mod.rs, one part line pair plus one row in hosted_agents_page.dart, one optional field in the hosted snapshot, one client and list method, one proof builder.
deltas.upstreamStatus: Provider-neutral client of a hosted provider route; not submitted to block/buzz.
deltas.removalCondition: Drop when hosted providers re-link agents during key rotation without an owner action, or upstream ships an equivalent owner-key re-link flow.

deltas.purpose: Owner attestation of agents a hosted provider minted ("every agent on Buzz"), and attaching a new hosted identity to an existing provider agent, desktop and mobile. The provider's POST /owner/agents/list answer now carries status (active | pending_attestation), kiingo_agent_id (validated lowercase UUID, otherwise dropped) and display_name per agent; an older answer without status reads as active, any other value as unknown (neither pending nor stale). The UI keys pending, paused and stale off status, never off desired_state (a pending agent's desired_state reads paused). Provider agent ids pass back verbatim (never trimmed or re-cased); an id with surrounding whitespace or control characters is not usable. Pending agents are attested through POST /owner/agents/attest-pending with exactly the re-link body (one fresh request id, one NIP-OA owner attestation per agent and no other, 1-20 agents) and the same fresh single-use kind-27236 buzz-provider-owner-v1 proof with action=attest_pending, provider, request, agent="", community, payload and expires; answers are bound to the request id, the current key and exactly the requested agents (activated | already_active | rejected, dm_opened; an omitted agent is a retryable result_missing; a dm_open_failed note on an activated agent is kept and shown as linked, since the provider retries the DM). Desktop signs natively and refuses to sign any agent the most recent authenticated list for the same signed-in key and community did not report as pending. An owner setting "Auto-link my new agents" (off by default, stored per signed-in key on the device: desktop localStorage, mobile SharedPreferences) runs a pass on launch, on resume (at most once a minute) and every 15 minutes while the app is in the foreground, never two at once: list, attest every pending agent, re-link every agent still on an earlier owner key through rebind-owner-key, in batches of at most 20, stopping at a whole-request failure; agents refused for good are remembered in memory per key so a pass does not sign for them again and are reported once with the reason in plain words; one quiet note (desktop toast, mobile SnackBar) names the agents it linked. With the setting off, each pending or stale agent has its own Link button that signs for that agent only. Attach: POST /owner/agents/unlinked (list-shaped read-only proof, action=list_unlinked) lists the owner's agents without a Buzz identity (kiingo_agent_id, display_name, owner_principal_type; machine defaults, malformed entries and repeats hidden; at most 200, newest first). The create form offers them under "Agent" with "Create a new agent" as the default (desktop: single-agent create dialog only, for the bundled destination; mobile: hosted create page). Mobile sends kiingo_agent_id on the create body and folds it into the idempotency key only when present. Desktop passes attachAgentId on the create request; the native create validates it (lowercase UUID) before side effects and remembers it beside the agent store (hosted-agent-attach.json, keyed by agent pubkey, pruned to known agents), and every deploy payload of that identity carries agent.kiingo_agent_id so replays and rollback keep the same idempotency key. Attach, ownership and service-setup codes (already_has_buzz_identity, not_agent_owner, agent_spec_required, kiingo_agent_id_invalid, provisioning_keys_*, scope_unconfigured) read as plain sentences in both apps. Hooks: command registrations plus re-exports in lib.rs/extensions/mod.rs, one import and one element in AppShell.tsx (same seam as the identity-rotation extension), one optional request field (requests.rs), one validate and one remember call in create (agents.rs), one apply call in the deploy payload builder (agents_deploy.rs), one optional attachAgentId through BackendIntent/WhereToRunDraft/CreateManagedAgentInput/createManagedAgent, one opt-in picker slot in WhereToRunSection.tsx enabled from AgentDialog.tsx, one wording seam in failedRemoteCreateMessage, one wrapper around HomePage in mobile app.dart, one section and part line in hosted_agents_page.dart, Link rows in agent_sections.dart, and optional fields in the hosted snapshot and draft.
deltas.upstreamStatus: Provider-neutral client of a hosted provider route; not submitted to block/buzz.
deltas.removalCondition: Drop when hosted providers activate agents without an owner attestation from the owner's device, or upstream ships an equivalent owner attestation flow.

deltas.purpose: Desktop "Agent" section in an agent's profile panel for a viewer who has a 1:1 DM with that agent, matching the mobile details card (#233): About, Runs on (harness · model · effort, "(pinned)"), For you (the resolved model and effort, or a plain reason: connect your <harness> subscription, or not available with your connected accounts), Where (machine name, a connected machine, or hosted compute), Your session (title · N turns), Owner (display name, "Your organization" for an Organization principal), skills, Tools (MCP tools, full or standard trust), and an "Edit agent" row opened in the browser, https only, shown only when edit_url is set. The cache is cleared in resetCommunityState(). DM-open prewarm (matching mobile #236): when a 1:1 agent DM opens, a fire-and-forget NIP-98 POST /agents/<agent pubkey>/prewarm with an empty body (no payload tag), at most once per agent per two minutes through a module-level map cleared in resetCommunityState(); the answer and any error are ignored and nothing retries. Hooks: one module plus re-export in extensions/mod.rs, one use line and two command registrations in lib.rs, one element in UserProfilePanelSections.tsx, the prewarm element beside the sessions picker in ChannelScreenHeader.tsx, and two reset lines in useCommunityInit.ts.

deltas.purpose: Desktop 1:1 agent calls from an agent DM: a proper voice call with the agent through its host's voice core (WebRTC between the webview and the host's realtime voice provider, the host answering the SDP offer), not a huddle. A Call button beside the sessions picker in a 1:1 agent DM header (known agents only) starts the call with the agent key and the DM channel id; the host answers only after proving the signer is the verified requester of that private 1:1 DM with the agent (never channels, group DMs or guests). Every request goes through one native command, agent_voice_request, that signs NIP-98 (kind 27235, exact URL with query, method, SHA-256 payload of the exact body) as the signed-in user with X-Buzz-Community, reaches only the host's call routes under <guest route origin>/api/buzz-voice/desktop (allowlisted paths, https only, 35 s timeout, size caps, no redirects) and returns {status, body}. The call controller is a port of the host's web call controller: mic with echo cancellation, an oai-events data channel, the time limit, a 5 s disconnect grace, mute, stop the agent's work, hang-up that never cancels work, and the host's call screen feed long-polled (wait 20 s, 1 s to 15 s backoff) for asks, the open question's option taps, per-ask cancel and archive (feed v2) and the post-call recap (followed at most 90 s after hang-up). The dock is mounted once in AppShell; a community switch hangs up and clears it (resetCommunityState()). Hooks: one module plus re-export in extensions/mod.rs, one use item and one command registration in lib.rs, one element and import in ChannelScreenHeader.tsx, one element and import in AppShell.tsx, one reset line and import in useCommunityInit.ts, and the microphone usage string in Info.plist. One audio owner: a call refuses while a huddle is active or starting (a probe registered by the audio-owning HuddleProvider, then the native huddle state, checked before and after the mic opens), and HuddleContext.tsx refuses huddle start and join while a call is busy (one import, one probe registration effect, one guard line in each of startHuddle and joinHuddle). Calls still connecting after 20 s end as media_failed. The native command parses the request URL once, checks its normalised path, and signs and sends that same URL; ask ids reject escapes of dot, slash and backslash; answers are capped at 2 MiB by declared length and while read; BUZZ_DESKTOP_AGENT_VOICE_URL and the shared HTTP-loopback allowance in guest_access.rs apply to debug builds only. A call also refuses (fails closed) when the huddle state can't be read. No Call button for agents managed on this device, and none until the local inventory has loaded.
deltas.upstreamStatus: Generic mechanism configured by the build-time guest route URL; not yet proposed upstream.
deltas.removalCondition: Remove when block/buzz offers agent voice calls or the host stops serving the call routes.

deltas.purpose: iOS 1:1 agent calls from an agent DM, matching the desktop call: a proper voice call with the agent through its host's voice core (WebRTC to the host's realtime voice provider, the host answering the SDP offer), not a huddle. A Call action beside the sessions action in a 1:1 agent DM header (native navigation action and Flutter button) opens the call screen and starts the call with the agent key and the DM channel id; the host answers only after proving the signer is the verified requester of that private 1:1 DM with the agent. deltas.purpose: Relay mesh restart safety. A restarted relay keeps its address but mints a new runtime id, so the previous boot's unexpired ready record pointed at the relay itself; boot awaited a dial to it before binding health, which could run past the liveness budget and restart the pod in a loop. Mesh boot no longer waits on any dial (the reconcile loop dials in the background), each dial is bounded well under the liveness budget, membership refuses records for another runtime id at its own address and gossiped records whose heartbeat outlived the registry expiry, and peers with no sign of life for that long are dropped from the peer table. The SIGTERM handler is installed before any startup work, so a signal during startup is not dropped when the relay runs as PID 1; on shutdown the relay deletes its own ready record, drains and exits 0. The boot lifecycle tests restart a mesh-on relay at the same address twice and assert readiness within the probe budget and a clean SIGTERM exit.

deltas.purpose: Creator-admitted huddle backing channels. A kind 9007 tagged ["admission", "creator", <parent channel id>] (private, TTL-bound, creator an active parent member) fixes its mark at creation; no kind 9002 adds, changes or clears it. Only the creator puts (kind 9000, target must be an active parent member) or removes (kind 9001); members leave with kind 9022; parent owners and admins may still delete it (kind 9008). Audio admits the creator and creator-put members (invited_by stamped by the relay from the put's signer) while they stay in the parent, with no parent auto-add or open shortcut and nobody once expired; the periodic audio re-check enforces the same rule. A kind 9001 or 9022 on such a channel answers OK only after the member's local audio socket closed and the end was published to the other pods; otherwise the socket is force-dropped and the OK carries the warning "warning: live audio close not confirmed". Opaque call and epoch tags on puts are echoed in the kind 39002 roster as ["put", member, call, epoch]. The audio re-check retries an unreadable mark each tick and disconnects after three consecutive failures, and admission is re-checked after the socket is bound. Huddle service identities (BUZZ_HUDDLE_SERVICE_PUBKEYS, advertised in NIP-11 as huddle_service_pubkeys) run creator-admitted huddles without membership: NIP-98 POST /events only, marked kind 9007, kind 9000/9001/9008 on marked channels they created (puts for active parent members, member role only), and one kind 48100 then one kind 48103 per backing channel they created; everything else is refused, they are never admitted to audio and appear in no roster. Desktop and mobile render their huddle notices as system notices.
